description: 5 MECHATRONICS MINDS, DIVERSE IN SKILL SETS, UNIFIED IN ONE MISSION. DRIVEN BY CURIOSITY AND A PASSION FOR ENGINEERING, WE THRIVE ON TACKLING NEW CHALLENGES, EXPLORING BOLD IDEAS AND TURNIG CREATIVE THINKING INTO INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS. WE DONT JUST THINK OUTSIDE THE BOX- WE'RE READY TO THINK BEYOND EARTH.
summary: We developed AstroGuard AI, an offline-first, explainable health intelligence and decision-support web application designed for long-duration human spaceflight missions.Long-duration missions expose astronauts to five major interacting hazards—space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile/closed environments—while communication delays limit real-time ground medical support. AstroGuard AI addresses this challenge by bringing longitudinal crew health records, manual or imported observations, evidence-linked risk screening, and care guidance into a single local workflow that travels directly with the crew.This project is important because deep-space crews require transparent, self-contained tools to monitor physiological changes, understand underlying risk context, and prioritize human medical reviews without relying on constant Earth connectivity or opaque black-box diagnoses.
details:
How It Works & What It Does AstroGuard AI operates as a connected, five-stage decision-support workflow:

  1. Crew Medical Files: Stores local crew profiles, baselines, medical histories, conditions, and allergies.
  2. Observations & Data Integration: Supports manual health entries alongside structured CSV and JSON dataset imports featuring data previews, column mapping, and unit/provenance checks.
  3. Explainable Risk Screening: Evaluates longitudinal trends (such as heart rate, cardiovascular strain, bone/muscle deconditioning, visual health/SANS awareness, and sleep/fatigue) using transparent, rule-based warning topics linked to spaceflight research.
  4. Care Support & Assistant: Provides prevention, escalation, and recovery context, allowing users to inspect trends, compare mission scenarios, export reports, and ask plain-language questions through a built-in Health Assistant.
  5. Mission Readiness Review: Organizes crew members into a prioritized human medical-review queue (Priority Review, Review Before Assignment, More Data Needed, and No Demo Flags).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Offline Autonomy: Runs locally with local storage and requires no external sensors or continuous Earth connection, ensuring reliability during communication delays.
  • Traceability & Transparency: Links every observation and flag to understandable, source-backed evidence rather than opaque predictions, while clearly labeling fictional versus imported records.
  • Human-Led Decision Support: Makes the next health action clearer by highlighting who needs medical attention first and why, while strictly preserving human authority over final medical clearance and flight GO/NO-GO decisions.

Tools, Software & Hardware Used

  • Software & Architecture: Built as a software-only, browser-based web dashboard prototype utilizing an offline-first architecture with local storage.
  • Hardware: Requires no external hardware or physical sensors to operate.
  • Data & AI Tools: Incorporates CSV and JSON data ingestion pipelines, a plain-language health assistant, and fictional demonstration datasets. Application code and presentation materials were prepared with ChatGPT assistance.

Creativity & Innovation Rather than attempting to build an automated diagnostic engine or relying on unavailable real-time biometric hardware, AstroGuard AI reframes space medicine around explainable, evidence-linked triage. Combining mission scenario simulation (such as an Artemis Lunar Gateway Analog) with rule-based spaceflight risk indexing and a conversational plain-language assistant bridges complex aerospace medical literature with practical crew-level usability.

Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Safety Boundaries & Clinical Ethics: Explicitly designed as an educational decision-support prototype—not a diagnostic tool or automated flight certification system—ensuring qualified medical personnel retain final clearance authority.
  • Scientific Grounding & Caveats: Anchored risk themes and radiation logs in public research from NASA's Human Research Program and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), while explicitly noting scientific caveats (e.g., radiation dose logs are not direct disease probabilities).
  • Data Privacy & Transparency: Avoided real personal astronaut health data in favor of fictional profiles, enforced clear data-provenance labels, and identified future validation steps including security/privacy hardening, NASA dataset format verification, and clinical review.
